title: Allocate customer receipt evidence to agency fee statements
description: Reuse the repository's existing canonical customer-receipt evidence and explicitly allocate it to ERP-070 agency service-fee statements. Keep receipt, sales-invoice and agency-fee allocation dimensions separate. Do not create another receipt master, initiate or confirm real funds, infer links, post accounting, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation audits and reuses the existing canonical customer-receipt evidence and ERP-070 statements, leaving one receipt master, one agency statement register and one explicit allocation model.
Authorized users can allocate an eligible active customer-receipt evidence record to one or more recorded agency service-fee statements using persisted identifiers only.

The server requires authoritative Customer and currency compatibility and rejects unavailable or voided records, duplicate receipt and statement pairs, non-positive values and allocation above either the receipt's available amount or statement's unallocated amount.
Partial allocation, one-to-many and many-to-one allocation are supported while unallocated receipt and statement amounts remain separately visible and are never silently written off.
Different currencies are never combined or converted unless an authoritative persisted conversion already belongs to the source evidence; no current or guessed exchange rate is used.
Allocation rows preserve receipt, statement and Customer snapshots, allocated amount, recorder and recorded time; client-supplied snapshots, balances and audit fields are not trusted.
An incorrect allocation can be voided with a bounded reason while preserving its original values and history; hard deletion, reassignment and silent amount replacement are not provided.
Sales-order receipt allocations, sales-invoice allocations and agency-statement allocations remain distinct evidence dimensions and are not added together as if they represented separate receipts.
Missing allocations are displayed as none or unknown and are not interpreted as unpaid, paid, settled, overdue, recognized revenue or posted status.
Creating, reading or voiding an allocation does not change receipt evidence, statement status, agreements, source orders or containers, Customer balances, bank, tax, finance or settlement records.
Queries and summaries are bounded and avoid per-row access; schema changes are idempotent and validation uses only permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit and integration tests cover partial and full allocation, multiple statements and receipts, Customer and currency mismatch, duplicate and over-allocation rejection, void history, unavailable records, bounded summaries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is deferred during development.

scenarios: Allocate one existing customer-receipt evidence record partially across two compatible recorded agency fee statements and verify separate remaining amounts without changing any source record or initiating funds movement.
Attempt duplicate, excessive, Customer-mismatched and currency-mismatched allocations, verify rejection, then void a valid allocation and confirm its original values and reason remain in history.

human_gate.reason: Explicit allocation of existing repository evidence only. Real receipt handling, bank access, accounting posting, production database mutation, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
